description_full: Clearfield, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, and distributes fiber management, protection, and delivery products in the United States and internationally. The company offers FieldSmart, a series of panels, cabinets, wall boxes, and other enclosures; WaveSmart, an optical component integrated for signal coupling, splitting, termination, multiplexing, demultiplexing, and attenuation for integration within its fiber management platform; and FiberFlex, an outdoor active cabinet for mounting and configuration of electronic equipment. It also provides CraftSmart FiberFirst pedestals, an access terminal that offers cable management and mounting bracket kit that support the deployment of access terminals; YOURx, an access terminal that provides flexibility with cable mid-span and internal splicing options; FieldShield, a fiber pathway and protection method for reducing the cost of broadband deployment; Fiber Assemblies used for industry-standard or customer-specified configurations; and ClearPass Connector Cleaning Dust Cap, which simplifies fiber connector cleaning while enhancing network performance. In addition, the company offers fiber to the premise, fiber to the business, DC interconnect/campus network, meet-me room, main distribution area, and white space. Further, it provides metro core, backhaul, indoor/outdoor DAS, small cells, and FTT-cell site. The company serves various service providers, including national carriers, community broadband, multiple system operators, legacy build-to-print copper and fiber assemblies, large enterprises, and original equipment manufacturer markets. It sells its products through sales force and authorized distributors. The company was formerly known as APA Enterprises, Inc. and changed its name to Clearfield, Inc. in January 2008. Clearfield, Inc. was incorporated in 1979 and is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.

financial_summary: Clearfield, Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $389M market cap on $150M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -18% over the past three years and +10% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.
Returns on capital run at 20% against a 11% cost of capital — a 9-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 41%.
The business throws off $22M in free cash flow — roughly 15 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
Accruals are elevated at -11.3% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 40× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 4.3% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insiders hold 18% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.

sect: Its 1% operating margin trails the Technology median (7%) by 6pp, so it is a below-average operator in its field.
It captures well under its share of sector profits (0.06x its revenue share).
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-34.9% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 530 companies in the universe; the top four hold 29% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the bottom of its 52-week range, 46% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 63% and a beta of 1.26, it amplifies market moves.
About $3.9M trades a day, enough to build a position.

val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $23.13 (margin of safety -24%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 21%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $17.86 to $31.09 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Technology peers: cheaper on P/FCF 17.8 vs 25.4, richer on P/E 53.0 vs 26.7 and EV/EBITDA 52.2 vs 16.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 498% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are mixed: an FCF yield of 5.6% (above the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 0.7% (vs the 8% bar).
The 4 covering analysts target $40.25 on average, 41% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 20% clears the cost of capital of 11.0% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.76).
It runs a 41% gross margin and converts 15% of revenue into free cash flow, or 11% after stock compensation.
Earnings quality is a concern: cash conversion of only -3.30x and high accruals (-11.3% of assets).
It spends 1.6% of revenue on R&D and 3.1% on stock compensation (above the 2% gate).
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $95.7M.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 6.3, in the safe zone).
Working capital ties up about 172 days of sales, a drag on cash generation.
growth: Revenue has compounded at -17.9% over 3 years, 10.0% over 5 years and 9.5% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 30%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded 35.1% a year over five years.
Capex runs only 0.8x depreciation (3.2% of sales), so the asset base is being harvested rather than grown.
Its Rule of 40 score is 21, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
It has missed earnings estimates by 123.5% on average.
own: Insiders own 18.2%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 69%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (8 sales, net $1.2M sold).
It returns 4.3% a year to shareholders (4.3% in buybacks).
Short interest is elevated at 11.7% of the float, 9.6 days to cover.
people: With about 243 employees, each generates about $618K of revenue, 1.7x the Technology median, and productivity has risen 10.9% a year.
That works out to $90K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $613K (1x revenue per employee).
